provisions.title: Genetic Information Privacy Act: direct-to-consumer genetic testing company requirements
provisions.quote: Obtain a consumer's consent for collecting, using or disclosing the consumer's genetic data, including: (a) Initial express consent that clearly describes the uses of the genetic data collected through the genetic testing product or service
provisions.appliesTo: "Direct-to-consumer genetic testing company" or "company" means an entity that offers genetic testing products or services directly to consumers (44-8001). Chapter does not apply to "Protected health information that is collected by a covered entity or business associate" (44-8003).

provisions.title: Genetic Information Privacy Act: separate consent to transfer or disclose
provisions.quote: (b) Separate express consent for any of the following: (i) Transferring or disclosing the consumer's genetic data to any person other than the company's vendors and service providers.
provisions.appliesTo: Direct-to-consumer genetic testing companies only (44-8001, paragraph 4).

provisions.title: Genetic Information Privacy Act: definitions
provisions.quote: "Express consent" means a consumer's affirmative response to a clear and prominent notice regarding collecting, using or disclosing genetic data for a specific purpose.
provisions.appliesTo: "Consumer" means an individual who is a resident of this state.

provisions.title: Session law adding the Genetic Information Privacy Act
provisions.quote: AMENDING TITLE 44, ARIZONA REVISED STATUTES, BY ADDING CHAPTER 38; RELATING TO GENETIC TESTING COMPANIES.
provisions.appliesTo: No effective date clause; 2021 general effective date 09-29-2021 per https://www.azleg.gov/general-effective-dates/

provisions.quote: Except as otherwise provided in state or federal law, an individual has the right to opt out of having the individual's individually identifiable health information accessible through a health information organization by providing notice as explained in the health information organization's notice of health information practices.
provisions.appliesTo: Health information organizations and participating health care providers.

provisions.quote: a person who receives HIV-related information in the course of providing a health service or pursuant to a release of HIV-related information shall not disclose that information to another person or legal entity
provisions.appliesTo: Persons receiving HIV-related information; does not apply to "persons or entities that are subject to regulation under title 20" (36-664(K)).

genetic.note: 12-2802 makes genetic test information confidential and privileged. 44-8002 bars DTC genetic testing companies from disclosing genetic data to insurers or employers. 12-2804(B) bars state agencies and local health authorities from releasing genetic testing information; it is recorded undated.

provisions.title: Communicable disease information; private right of action
provisions.quote: A protected person may bring an action in superior court for legal and equitable relief on his own behalf against a person who violates this article.
provisions.appliesTo: Violations of title 36, chapter 6, article 4 (communicable disease related information, including HIV). Not applicable to entities regulated under title 20 (36-664(K)).

provisions.quote: A knowing and wilful violation of this section is an unlawful practice pursuant to section 44-1522, and only the attorney general may enforce such a violation

provisions.title: Genetic Information Privacy Act enforcement
provisions.quote: The attorney general may bring an action to enforce this chapter.
provisions.appliesTo: Direct-to-consumer genetic testing companies; civil penalty up to $2,500 per violation.

provisions.title: Medical records; good-faith immunity
provisions.quote: A health care provider, contractor or clinical laboratory that acts in good faith under this article is not liable for damages in any civil action for the disclosure of medical records
provisions.appliesTo: Medical records article (12-2291 et seq.); no private right of action stated in 12-2292 or 12-2296.
